note: Start here if you've never been under the hood before.

items.title: Nand to Tetris
items.desc: Build a working computer from logic gates up to a running app. The single best way to actually understand how computers work.

items.title: CS50: Intro to Computer Science
items.desc: Harvard's famous free intro course. covers computing fundamentals from the ground up, no prior experience needed.

items.title: Crash Course Computer Science
items.desc: 40-episode YouTube series covering everything from binary to the internet, fast and visual.

note: Actually writing code, for the first time or the fifth.

items.title: freeCodeCamp
items.desc: Full curriculum from HTML basics to full-stack projects, entirely free, with real certificates.

items.title: The Odin Project
items.desc: Project-based full-stack web dev path. Less hand-holding than freeCodeCamp, closer to real work.

items.title: Automate the Boring Stuff with Python
items.desc: Free online book teaching Python through practical, useful scripts instead of abstract theory.

items.title: MIT 6.100L: Intro to CS with Python
items.desc: MIT OpenCourseWare's intro programming course, lecture videos and problem sets included.

items.title: Material Design Guidelines
items.desc: Google's free, detailed design system documentation. covers color, typography, layout, and components with real reasoning behind each rule.

items.title: Laws of UX
items.desc: Short, visual breakdowns of the psychology principles behind good design decisions.

items.title: Figma's Design 101 (YouTube)
items.desc: Free video series covering design fundamentals directly from the tool most teams design in.

note: Statistics, machine learning, and working with data.

items.title: Khan Academy: Statistics & Probability
items.desc: Free, structured, and the most common recommendation for building real statistical intuition from scratch.

items.title: fast.ai: Practical Deep Learning
items.desc: Teaches deep learning by building working models first, theory second. made for people who learn by doing.

items.title: 3Blue1Brown: Neural Networks
items.desc: The best visual explanation of how neural networks actually work, no heavy math background assumed.

note: Money, markets, and how businesses actually run.

items.title: Khan Academy: Personal Finance
items.desc: Covers budgeting, saving, credit, and investing basics in plain language, completely free.

items.title: Y Combinator's Startup School
items.desc: Free lecture series on building and running an early-stage company, taught by people who've actually done it.

note: Picking up a new spoken or written language.

items.title: Duolingo
items.desc: The most accessible starting point for daily language practice. free, gamified, works on mobile.

items.title: BBC Learning English
items.desc: Still active and free daily lessons, grammar, and listening practice from the BBC, though focused on English specifically rather than multiple languages.

note: Fundamentals for anyone starting from a blank page.

items.title: Drawabox
items.desc: A completely free, structured curriculum built around drawing fundamentals, lines, perspective, form. with homework and a community that critiques your work.

items.title: Proko
items.desc: Free figure drawing and anatomy lessons from a former Watts Atelier instructor. the most recommended starting point for drawing people.

items.title: Ctrl+Paint
items.desc: Free video lessons on digital painting fundamentals, value, color, and composition aimed at total beginners.

note: Circuits, components, and building things that actually light up.

items.title: All About Circuits
items.desc: A free, textbook-depth online reference covering electronics from basic DC theory up to semiconductors. the internet's most-cited free electronics resource.

items.title: Ben Eater: Building an 8-bit computer
items.desc: A YouTube series building a working computer on breadboards from individual logic chips. genuinely teaches electronics and computer architecture at once.

items.title: Khan Academy: Electrical Engineering
items.desc: Free structured lessons on circuits, currents, and components, building up from first principles.

note: How things actually leave the ground.

items.title: NASA: Beginner's Guide to Rockets
items.desc: NASA's own free, plain-language guide to rocket propulsion and flight, written for students and hobbyists.

items.title: Everyday Astronaut
items.desc: A YouTube channel that explains real rocket engineering, engines, staging, re-entry in accessible, highly detailed video essays.

items.title: MIT OCW: Unified Engineering (Aerospace)
items.desc: MIT's real aerospace engineering coursework, made free through OpenCourseWare. lecture notes, problem sets, and exams included.

note: Where mechanics, electronics, and code meet.

items.title: Underactuated Robotics (MIT)
items.desc: A free, real MIT course on the math and control theory behind robots that move. lecture videos, notes, and an online textbook, taught by Russ Tedrake.

items.title: MIT OCW: Introduction to Robotics
items.desc: Free lecture notes and assignments covering the fundamentals of how robots sense, plan, and move.

note: Making beats, mixing, and understanding your DAW.

items.title: Ableton: Learning Music
items.desc: A free, interactive site by Ableton itself that teaches rhythm, melody, and chords by letting you play with them directly in the browser.

items.title: In The Mix (YouTube)
items.desc: Free, detailed tutorials on mixing, mastering, and music production workflow, covering multiple DAWs.

note: Building an actual playable game from scratch.

items.title: CS50's Introduction to Game Development
items.desc: Harvard's free course teaching 2D game development principles by rebuilding classic games.

items.title: Brackeys (YouTube)
items.desc: One of the most recommended free Unity tutorial libraries ever made, still fully available and relevant for beginners.
